texts: Where the scales of effort are laid down, union comes as ease, as breath comes, with no weighing and no force.
scales, effortless union
doha with scales about reaching God without any struggle or austerity

Compose a doha about a seeker who spent years weighing his austerities on scales and found no peace, until he stopped trying and discovered the effortless state of union that was always there, natural as breathing.
I counted my fasts and hours of meditation like grains on a pair of scales, and only when I gave up the counting did a quiet ease settle over me without my doing anything.
weaver's loom, effortless union
Write a doha about a weaver whose cloth takes shape on the loom without strain once he stops forcing his hands, just as the effortless state of union comes naturally to the one who stops forcing.
doha with a weaver's loom about easy natural union with God
The shuttle glides, the cloth grows, and the weaver forgets himself: so union comes, effortless and unforced.
My uncle has woven at his loom for forty years, and he says that when his mind stops straining the work flows by itself, and that is as close to God as he has been.
No austerity, no force, no scaling of cold heights; the Beloved is simply here, in the ease of being.
natural union, no effort
I spent years in harsh fasts and rigid practices, then one quiet afternoon stopped everything and found I was already content, with no struggle, as if I had arrived without moving.
doha about the easy natural state of oneness that needs no struggle
I would like a doha that says the highest state is not won by hard penance or force, but is the simple, natural, effortless state of being at one with the Lord, which was never lost.
doha with a market and a bee about being in union while living normally
market, bee, effortless oneness
Write a doha about a man in a noisy market, humming like a bee at its work, who lives in union with the Lord without any austerity, naturally and easily, in the middle of ordinary life.
My father runs a stall in the market all day, hums to himself like a bee, never meditates and never fasts, yet there is an easy calm about him that I have never seen in anyone who tried hard.
In the market's noise the bee hums on, and the heart rests in the Lord without effort, as a bee rests in honey.

Please write a doha about a hermit who wrapped himself in a thin cloth sheet and starved himself on harsh austerities, and a beggar who simply sat at ease and found the Lord in his natural state, without any force.
A beggar who sleeps under a cloth sheet outside the station told me he has never practised anything, yet he seems more at peace than the monks who torture themselves with penance.
The hermit tied himself to harsh vows, the beggar sat with his cloth sheet at ease, and union found the beggar.
cloth sheet and beggar doha - union is natural, not forced by penance
cloth sheet, beggar, ease
No bridge of penance is needed to cross to the Beloved, for He stands already at the near bank.
bridge, effortless union
I kept building elaborate disciplines like a bridge toward some distant peace, until I stopped and noticed the peace had been sitting on my side of the water all along.
doha with a bridge - union with God needs no hard effort
Compose a doha about a bridge that people strain to build across the water to reach God, when the seeker at ease knows the Lord is already on this bank, reached by ease and not by force.
After years of rigid routines and harsh self-discipline that only made me tense, I let it all go on holiday and found, to my surprise, a simple stillness I had been chasing the whole time.
easy, natural, no force
doha on the effortless natural union with God, no austerity needed
Please write a doha about a seeker who has tried every discipline and every austerity and found them all hard and joyless, until he relaxed into the simple natural state which needs no effort at all.
Let go the reins, let the breath be breath: union with the Lord is not made but remembered.
moth doha - union that happens naturally, no force, no struggle
Write a doha about a moth that does not plan or strive but simply drifts toward the light, so the soul moves effortlessly into union with the Lord, without penance or force, by its own nature.
moth, effortless union
The moth does not climb to the light by effort; it is drawn as water is drawn downhill, with ease.
Watching a moth drift toward our porch light without any effort or hesitation, I wondered why my own search for peace had always been such hard work.
At the mosque, I watched a very old man pray without any strain, with a face so simple and easy that I felt he was already in union with God, while the young men worked so hard at it.
mosque, effortless oneness
Write a doha about a mosque full of men straining at hard rites, and one old man who simply sits at ease in the natural, effortless state of union with the Lord, needing no force at all.
doha with a mosque on easy natural union, no force or hard penance
Let the mosque echo with efforts and rules; the soul rests in the Lord's presence as easily as in its own breath.
scales and market doha about union that can't be bought or earned by weighing deeds
In the market the shopkeeper weighs everything on scales, but my grandmother, who never sat in meditation, lives in an easy union with God that she never had to earn.
The market weighs, the scales tip, but union cannot be weighed; it is the ease of the heart as it is.
scales, market, natural ease

Compose a doha about a market where everything is weighed on scales, and a quiet soul who knows that union with the Lord is not earned by weighing deeds, but is the natural, effortless state of the heart.
My yoga teacher kept telling us to push harder into difficult poses, and the only time I felt true peace was in the final rest, when I did nothing at all.
When the effort ends, the Beloved begins; the easy breath is the sweetest worship.
I want a doha about the state beyond all effort, where the seeker neither fasts nor strains nor fights, but simply rests in the Lord as water rests in water, easy and natural.
effortless union, no striving
doha for people tired of hard spiritual practice: it's natural and easy

Compose a doha about the philosopher's stone that transforms without effort and a temple built with great struggle, saying the true union with the Lord is effortless and natural, found by ease and not by force.
philosopher's stone, temple, ease
My grandfather exhausted himself building a temple and hunting for a philosopher's stone, and only in his last years, doing nothing special, did he seem truly united with God.
The temple takes a hundred years, the philosopher's stone a thousand vows; union takes a single easy breath.
doha with a philosopher's stone and a temple, union is natural, not forced
The arrow flies straight when the archer does not strain; so the soul reaches the Lord with ease.
Please write a doha about an archer who releases his arrow in perfect ease, without straining or aiming too hard, and about the soul that reaches the Lord in the same effortless way.
My archery teacher says the best arrow flies when you stop trying to make it happen, and I thought: that is how my own peace finally came.
arrow, effortless union
arrow doha about reaching God naturally, without force
The swan glides on the lake without a single stroke of effort; so the soul glides into union.
On a calm lake I watched a swan glide across without any sign of effort, and I thought how I had spent my life paddling hard against a current that was not there.
swan doha about easy natural union with the divine
swan, easy union
Write a doha about a swan that rests on the surface of the lake without strain, as the soul rests in the natural state of union with the Lord, needing no austerity, no force and no effort.

Please write a doha about a cuckoo that sings freely from its branch near the cremation ground, untroubled by what lies below, in the effortless natural state of union that needs neither austerity nor force.
My grandmother lived next to the cremation ground for forty years, and a cuckoo sang there each spring; she was the most easy and effortlessly peaceful person I have ever known.
The cuckoo sings beside the cremation ground, untroubled and unforced, and the song is the Lord's own ease.
doha with a cuckoo and a cremation ground about easy natural oneness
cuckoo, cremation ground, ease
Neither fast nor vigil, neither force nor effort; the Lord is found in the ease of simply being.
I used to think enlightenment meant hard discipline, but when I finally stopped trying to achieve it, I found I was already living in a quiet that needed no effort.
union without effort
doha about how union with God is easy and natural, no hard practice
Compose a doha about the sahaj state in which a person lives at ease, neither forcing nor resisting, in natural union with the Lord, free of all austerity, discipline and strain.
When the mind stops straining, the heart is home: union is the nature of the quiet one.
ease, no effort, oneness
doha on the easy, effortless natural state of oneness with God
Write a doha for a person weary of hard spiritual practices who is told that the highest state is no state of strain at all, but the simple, natural, effortless ease of being united with the Lord.
After years of hard retreats and silent rules, I drifted into a sunny afternoon one day, and for the first time felt the union I had been chasing, with no strain or fuss.
Sitting beneath a date palm after a long walk, I stopped striving to feel anything, and a deep easy contentment rose by itself, as natural as the shade.
The date palm bears sweet fruit without trying; so the soul in union bears peace without effort.
doha with a date palm about natural union, no force or austerity
Compose a doha about a date palm that bears fruit without strain, as the soul in its natural state of union with the Lord bears peace without austerity, force or effort, simply by being what it is.
date palm, effortless union
The oil press groans and strains to squeeze its drop; union asks no pressing, only the ease of being.
oil press, effortless union
Write a doha about an oil press that must strain and crush to give its oil, while the soul's union with the Lord needs no pressing, no austerity and no force, only its own easy, natural stillness.
My uncle works the oil press till his back aches, and he says that his only moments of true peace come on the day of rest when he does absolutely nothing.
oil press doha - union with God needs no pressing or effort
crow, tree, easy oneness
The crow sits in the tree without a plan; so the soul rests in the Lord, simply and without struggle.
A crow sat on the branch of the tree outside my window all morning doing nothing at all, and I envied how perfectly at ease it was.
Please write a doha about a crow resting in the shade of a tree with no worries or effort, as the soul rests in the Lord in its natural state, without any austerity, force or planning.
crow and tree doha about the easy way of being at one with God
needle, effortless union
The needle slips through the cloth when the hand is gentle; so the soul slips into union without force.
doha with a needle - union comes with ease, not by forcing it
Compose a doha about a needle that passes through cloth smoothly when the tailor stops forcing, as the soul passes into union with the Lord effortlessly when it ends its striving and austerities.
My grandmother sews perfectly with her needle when she is relaxed but pricks herself when she hurries, and she says the spirit is the same: it works with ease or not at all.
Not by the strain of will or the labour of penance, but by the quiet ease of being, is the Beloved found.
I want a doha about the effortless state of being at one with the Lord, which cannot be forced by willpower or austerity but arises when the seeker stops striving and simply rests in what is.
ease, rest, oneness
doha about reaching God by relaxing into it, not forcing it
I tried every technique for years, and finally the only thing that worked was allowing myself to sit with nothing to achieve, and the stillness arrived on its own.
Write a doha about a temple where devotees exhaust themselves with vows and austerities, while a quiet man outside sits at ease in the natural state of union with the Lord and needs no force.
The temple demands vows and vigils; union asks only that the heart be at ease.
temple doha - you don't need hard penance, union is natural
At the temple fair people were doing painful vows and walking barefoot on hot ground, but the old pujari's cook, laughing and relaxed, looked far closer to God.
temple, effortless union
parrot and cloth sheet doha - union comes easy when you stop trying
My neighbour's parrot repeats prayers without effort while the man sits wrapped in a cloth sheet, doing nothing, and somehow he is the calmest person I know.

Write a doha about a parrot that repeats the Name without strain, and a seeker in a plain cloth sheet who sits at ease, showing that union with the Lord is natural and effortless, requiring no austerity.
parrot, cloth sheet, ease
The parrot says the Name, the cloth sheet wraps the quiet, and the heart rests in the Lord, effortlessly.
After years of working at meditation with clenched effort, I woke one morning and noticed that the pearl of peace had been sitting in my hand all along, requiring no seeking.
Compose a doha about a pearl that lies in the shell without any effort on its part, as the soul lies in union with the Lord without austerity or force, naturally, by its own deep nature.
pearl, effortless oneness
pearl doha about easy natural union with God
The pearl does not strive to shine; it shines because it is a pearl, and so shines the soul in the Lord.
The furnace at the steel mill is so hot that the workers burn themselves out, but a stone mason I know works at a gentle pace and says that is how he finds God.
The furnace burns, the stone is hammered; yet the soul rests in the Lord untouched by either, easily.
Please write a doha about a furnace that forces iron into shape and a stone that is chiselled with great effort, while the soul's union with the Lord needs no force at all and comes naturally.
furnace, stone, ease
furnace and stone doha - union with the divine needs no struggle
When I stopped trying so hard to feel spiritual, I noticed the thing I wanted had been present all along, in ordinary moments of chores and walking.

Compose a doha about the way the highest union is found in ordinary moments of eating, walking and breathing, without any special practice, in the easy, natural, unforced state of simply being what we are.
doha about reaching God in ordinary life, no special practices needed
ordinary life, effortless union
Eating, walking, sleeping, waking: all of it is worship when the heart is at ease in the Lord.
The priest chants with a straining voice; the quiet heart is united with the Lord without a single word.
The priest at our local gathering strains through long rituals, but my quiet aunt who sits in the corner doing nothing seems to be the one actually at peace.
priest doha - union with God is easy and natural, not forced by ritual
Write a doha about a priest who exhausts himself with elaborate rituals and austerities, while the simple soul beside him sits at ease and is already one with the Lord, without any force.
priest, effortless union
traveler and palace doha - union is natural, no hard journey needed
traveler, palace, ease
I journeyed across the world as a traveler to a palace-turned-retreat to find peace, and found it only on the last evening, when I stopped trying and just sat there at ease.
Please write a doha about a traveler who walks far to a grand palace to find the Lord, and discovers that union is not at the end of any journey, but is the easy, natural state already within.
The traveler seeks the palace gate; but union is not a place, it is the ease of the one who has stopped walking.
Write a doha about a shroud that wraps the dead and the strain of a lifetime of austerities, saying the Lord's union was never about effort and can be had at ease, now, while alive, naturally.
The shroud will wrap the strained and the easy alike; the soul that lives at ease in the Lord has already crossed.
shroud, effortless union
shroud doha - union is natural and easy, why strain for it
My grandfather prepared his shroud years in advance with great ceremony, but his actual peace came in his last year, when he gave up all discipline and simply enjoyed each day.
Where there is no striving, there is the Lord; sit, and the mind will settle like silt in still water.
I spent years in tense effort at being spiritual, and relief came on an ordinary evening when I let it all drop and felt a stillness that required nothing of me.
stillness, no striving
I would like a doha that says the soul's natural condition is peace and union with the Lord, and that no austerity or force can create it, only the ease of letting go of all effort.
doha about the easy, natural way to be one with God
The ash of burnt austerities lies cold; the Lord is found in the warm ease of the unforced heart.
ash, effortless union
ash doha about natural union with God, no need for harsh penance
Compose a doha about an ascetic who smears himself with ash and starves himself on harsh austerities, while a laughing child in the lane is already in the effortless natural union he seeks.
The ash-smeared ascetic outside our village starves himself for years, but my little niece, who knows nothing of religion, laughs with an ease that seems closer to the divine.
I carried a heavy stone up the hill as a penance last year and felt nothing, then sat beside it afterward doing nothing and felt wonderfully close to something larger.
doha with a stone - union with God is natural, not a hard climb
stone, effortless union
Write a doha about a stone that sits at ease where it lies, without striving or aim, as the soul in the natural state of union with the Lord needs no austerity, no force and no journey.
The stone does not strive to stay; it rests, and the soul at rest in the Lord is likewise unmoving, easy.
cleric doha - union is natural and easy, not forced by hard rules
The cleric ties the faithful with vows, but the Beloved is found by the one who rests without strain.
Please write a doha about a cleric who binds the faithful with a hundred hard rules and austerities, when union with the Lord is the natural, easy state of the heart, found by ease, not by force.
The cleric in our locality demands such severe discipline of his followers that many look exhausted, while a quiet shopkeeper I know seems naturally and easily at peace with God.
cleric, effortless union
Compose a doha about a peacock dancing at ease and a fire that burns without being forced, to show that union with the Lord is also natural and spontaneous, requiring no austerity or effort of ours.
The peacock dances without a teacher, the fire burns without being told; so does the soul move into the Lord.
I watched a peacock dancing in the monsoon and a village bonfire burning by itself at night, and understood that the best things in life are spontaneous and not forced.
fire, peacock, spontaneity
doha with fire and a peacock about natural, spontaneous union
sun and leaf doha - union is natural, like a leaf turning to the sun
Write a doha about a leaf that turns toward the sun without effort or thought, as the soul turns to the Lord in its natural state, without austerity or force, simply because that is its nature.
The leaf on my desk plant leans toward the sun every day without any effort, and I thought: if only my spiritual life were that easy and natural.
The leaf turns to the sun without a plan; the soul turns to the Lord without a vow.
sun, leaf, effortless turning
After I stopped chasing achievements and spiritual goals, I discovered a quiet sweetness in simply being present at my own life, as though it was always there.
Put down the burden of becoming, and find that you already are what you sought, in the Lord.
I want a doha about the state of simple, easy union with the Lord that needs no goal, no technique and no force, because it is not something to be achieved but something already present.
already here, no striving
doha about how union with God is already here, no need to strive
crow and boat doha - union is easy, drifting not rowing
crow, boat, drifting oneness
Please write a doha about a boat that drifts with the current and a crow that rides on it without effort, showing the soul that rests in the Lord without strain, drifting in natural union.
On a ferry ride I watched a crow ride on the boat's roof all the way across, utterly relaxed, and I thought how little force it takes to arrive anywhere.
The boat drifts, the crow rests on its mast, and the Lord carries all who do not row against Him.
fish doha - union is as natural as a fish in water
Write a doha about a fish that swims in water without ever thinking about it, as the soul lives in the Lord without strain or austerity, as naturally as a fish in its element.
fish, natural oneness
My uncle, a fisherman, never thinks about how to swim and neither do the fish he catches, and he says that is how God should be known: without thinking.
The fish never seeks the water, yet lives in it; so is the soul in the Lord, effortlessly.
doha about letting things be and finding peace without trying
Compose a doha about a seeker who gave up all striving, all fasting and all hard effort, and found at last that the peace he sought was his natural condition, easy and always present.
When I finally stopped fighting my own restless mind and just let it be, the calm that settled in was greater than any I had forced through years of discipline.
let be, find peace
Let the wave be a wave and the mind be a mind; in not resisting, the Lord is found.
Sweet as the breath is union with the Lord, needing no practice but the remembering of what is.
Write a doha about the state of oneness with the Lord that is as natural as breathing, requiring no instrument, no austerity and no force, only the ease of recognizing what has always been so.
doha on union that's as easy and natural as breathing
Last night I noticed my own breath for the first time in years, and felt, with no effort at all, that I was being held by something larger.
breath, ease, oneness
yogi, effortless oneness
A yogi in our hill town gave up his hard postures and now sits laughing under the sky, and he says that is when he finally found what he had been searching for.
yogi doha - union is natural and easy, you can stop forcing it
The yogi unties his knotted limbs and finds the Lord waiting in the ease of his breath.
Write a doha about a yogi who struggled for decades with painful postures and finally relaxed, discovering the natural, effortless state of union with the Lord that required no force at all.
Write a doha about a weaver at his loom who works in effortless rhythm, neither forcing nor resisting, finding the natural union with the Lord in the simple ease of his craft.
My father works at his loom without any apparent effort, and when I asked how he stays so calm, he said the rhythm does the work and he just goes along.
weaver's loom doha about easy natural union with God
weaver's loom, ease
The loom hums and the weaver's mind goes still; in that hush, without effort, the Lord arrives.
Our fishing boat drifted all night after the engine failed, and in the quiet I heard a rainbird calling and felt a deep ease that I had never found through effort.

Please write a doha about a boat floating with no one rowing it and a rainbird singing from the shore, showing the state of ease in which the soul is united with the Lord without any force or struggle.
boat, rainbird, ease
The boat drifts and the rainbird sings; no one is rowing, and the Lord is near.
boat and rainbird doha - letting go and finding union naturally
The moneylender strains to count, the bell strains to ring, but the soul rests in the Lord with ease.
Compose a doha about a moneylender who strains all day over his accounts while a bell rings out on the hour, and the quiet soul beside them rests in effortless union with the Lord.
moneylender and bell doha - union is easy, not a hard task
The moneylender in my village works himself ragged and rings a bell to start each business day, but his quiet old mother, who does no practice, seems more in tune with God.
moneylender, bell, ease
Salt dissolves in water without effort; so the soul dissolves into the Lord, easily, entirely.
salt doha about merging with God naturally and without force
Write a doha about salt that dissolves into water without any strain or austerity, as the soul merges into the Lord in its natural, effortless state of union, leaving no trace of effort behind.
salt, effortless merging
I stirred salt into a glass of water and watched it vanish with no effort, and I thought how my own spiritual striving could have been as easy as that.
doha on the easy, natural way to find peace with God
Do nothing, force nothing, seek nothing, and the Beloved arrives of His own accord.
I used to think peace had to be fought for, but then I stopped trying on a quiet Sunday and noticed the contentment had been there waiting the whole time.
no effort, no force
Compose a doha for the weary seeker who has tried too hard and failed, telling him that union with the Lord is the easiest of all things, natural and simple, and asks nothing but ease.

Please write a doha about a beggar who sits at ease by the roadside without a worry in the world, enjoying the natural, effortless union with the Lord that kings and ascetics strive in vain to achieve.
beggar, effortless union
The beggar sits at ease while kings strain; the Lord rests in the heart that has nothing to achieve.
beggar doha about how natural and easy being one with God is
The beggar at the corner never meditates or fasts but seems so naturally content that I once found myself envying him more than the people who live by strict spiritual rules.
market, musk deer, effortless oneness
The market was loud and busy, yet a woman selling musk perfume sat in complete ease among it all, and I could tell she was naturally united with something deeper.
Write a doha about a musk deer that carries its own fragrance without effort, and a market full of strain, showing that union with the Lord is natural and needs no seeking, force or hard labour.
musk deer and market doha - union with God is natural, not forced
The musk deer never works to make its scent; so the soul in the Lord is fragrant without effort.
After the birth of my child, I stopped doing every spiritual practice I had forced myself through, and strangely found a continuous quiet joy that effort had never given me.

Compose a doha about the state of effortless union with the Lord that arrives not through disciplines or forced practice but through a natural softening of the heart, and remains in every ordinary moment.
ease, softness, union
doha on the effortless union that comes when you stop forcing the practice
When the heart grows soft as morning, the Lord moves in without a knock, and nothing is forced.
